requirements.quote:
A vector (single-dimensioned array) is a stream of homogeneous data
   elements.
requirements.condition: a field is encoded as a vector
requirements.required_behavior: encode every vector member as the same element type
requirements.forbidden_behavior: mix element types within one vector
requirements.why_checkable: Vector element decoding can be checked against the single declared element type.

requirements.quote:
In either case, the length
   declares the number of bytes, not the number of elements, in the
   vector.
requirements.condition: a vector definition or encoding declares a length
requirements.required_behavior: interpret the length as a byte count
requirements.forbidden_behavior: interpret the length as an element count
requirements.why_checkable: Vectors whose element width exceeds one byte distinguish byte-count and element-count implementations.

requirements.quote: Here, T' occupies n bytes in the data stream
requirements.condition: a fixed-length vector is declared as T T'[n]
requirements.required_behavior: encode and consume exactly n bytes for T'
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode or consume a different number of bytes
requirements.why_checkable: Fixed-vector serialization and parser consumption have an exact byte count.

requirements.quote:
where n is a multiple
   of the size of T.
requirements.condition: a fixed-length vector of element type T is declared with byte length n
requirements.required_behavior: require n to be an exact multiple of the encoded size of T
requirements.forbidden_behavior: define or accept a fixed vector ending with a partial element
requirements.why_checkable: The declared byte count and element width permit a direct divisibility check.

requirements.quote:
The length of the vector is not included in the
   encoded stream.
requirements.condition: a vector has a fixed length declared as T T'[n]
requirements.required_behavior: encode only the vector contents without a length field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: prepend or otherwise include the fixed vector's length in the encoded stream
requirements.why_checkable: The fixed-vector wire encoding can be checked for the absence of a length prefix.

requirements.quote:
Variable-length vectors are defined by specifying a subrange of legal
   lengths, inclusively, using the notation <floor..ceiling>.
requirements.condition: a variable-length vector is declared as T T'<floor..ceiling>
requirements.required_behavior: require its actual byte length to be between floor and ceiling inclusive
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept an actual length below floor or above ceiling
requirements.error_behavior: treat a length outside the inclusive range as illegal
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests can exercise floor minus one, floor, ceiling, and ceiling plus one.

requirements.quote:
When
   these are encoded, the actual length precedes the vector's contents
   in the byte stream.
requirements.required_behavior: encode its actual byte length in a length field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode a length field that does not describe the vector's actual content length
requirements.why_checkable: The declared length value can be compared with the number of following content bytes.

requirements.quote:
When
   these are encoded, the actual length precedes the vector's contents
   in the byte stream.
requirements.required_behavior: place the actual-length field immediately before the vector contents
requirements.forbidden_behavior: place the length after or within the vector contents
requirements.why_checkable: The byte offset of the length field relative to the vector contents is deterministic.

requirements.quote:
The length will be in the form of a number
   consuming as many bytes as required to hold the vector's specified
   maximum (ceiling) length.
requirements.condition: a variable-length vector has specified ceiling length
requirements.required_behavior: encode its length field using the number of bytes required to represent the ceiling
requirements.forbidden_behavior: choose the length-field width from the actual length or use a width too small for the ceiling
requirements.why_checkable: The ceiling deterministically fixes the length-prefix width for every instance.

requirements.quote:
A variable-length vector with an actual
   length field of zero is referred to as an empty vector.
requirements.condition: a variable-length vector's actual-length field is zero
requirements.required_behavior: decode the vector as empty with zero content bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: consume element bytes as part of that zero-length vector
requirements.why_checkable: A zero prefix has a deterministic decoded element count and parser offset.

requirements.quote:
Variable-length vectors are defined by specifying a subrange of legal
   lengths, inclusively, using the notation <floor..ceiling>.
requirements.condition: a variable-length vector has an actual length of zero
requirements.required_behavior: permit the empty vector only when the declared floor is zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept an empty vector when the declared floor is greater than zero
requirements.error_behavior: treat zero as an illegal length when it lies below floor
requirements.why_checkable: Applying the inclusive legal-length range to zero directly determines whether an empty vector is valid.

requirements.quote:
The length of an
   encoded vector must be an exact multiple of the length of a single
   element (e.g., a 17-byte vector of uint16 would be illegal).
requirements.condition: a vector's element type occupies more than zero bytes
requirements.required_behavior: require the encoded vector byte length to be an exact multiple of one element's encoded length
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept a vector containing a trailing partial element
requirements.error_behavior: treat a non-multiple vector length as illegal
requirements.why_checkable: The parser can compute length modulo element width and reject nonzero remainders.
